chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the woman approaches her menses while she is in a state of menstruation, let her perform the ritual bath (ghusl) and place cotton (kirsaf) in her private area, and let her stand with other women behind her so they affirm her supplication, and she should say: 'O Allah, I ask You by every Name that is Yours, or by which You named one of Your creatures, or by which You singled Yourself out in the Knowledge of the Unseen with You.'

And I ask You by Your Greatest Name, the Greatest, and by every letter You revealed to Moses, and by every letter You revealed to Jesus, and by every letter You revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), that You remove this blood from me.
And when she intends to enter the Sacred Mosque or the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), she should do the same.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And she should go to the place of Gabriel (peace be upon him), which is beneath the eaves, for it was his place when he sought permission from the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him). He said: That is a place wherein a menstruating woman does not supplicate to Allah, facing the Qiblah, and recite the supplication for the blood, except that she sees purity, if Allah wills.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ritual supplication and procedure for hastening the end of menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the ritual of *istishfa'* (hastening menstruation's end) through a specific supplication invoking Allah's Greatest Name and the divine letters revealed to Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad. It highlights the spiritual efficacy of performing this rite at Maqam Jibril beneath the Kaaba's eaves, a location traditionally associated with the Prophet's private audience with Gabriel, thereby linking physical purification with prophetic precedent. The practice underscores the Shia emphasis on intercessory supplication and the transformative power of divine names in alleviating natural bodily states.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bi nIbrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the woman comes to be upon her rituals, so let her wash and let her stuff herself with the cotton and she should pause with the (other) women behind her, so they would be saying ‘Ameen’ upon her supplication, and she should be saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!

I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> with every Name which is for You<sup>azwj</sup>, or You<sup>azwj</sup> are Named with for one of Your<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, or concealed within the hidden Knowledge with You<sup>azwj</sup>!

And, I ask You<sup>asws</sup> by the most Magnificent of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Magnificent Names, and by every Letter You<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto Musa<sup>as</sup>, and by every Letter You<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto Isa<sup>as</sup>, and by every Letter You<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> that this blood should go away from me.
And, when she intends to enter the Sacred Masjid, or Masjid of the Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, she should do similar to that.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And she should go to the place of Jibraeel<sup>as</sup>, and it is beneath the water sprout, for it was his<sup>as</sup> place when he<sup>as</sup> sought permission to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So that is a place wherein nor menstruating woman would supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, facing the Qiblah, and supplicate with the supplication for the blood, except that she would see purity, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’

When a woman experiences menses at a time when she is about to commence the acts of her al-Hajj, she should take a shower and use al-kursuf, stand up with women behind her who should say ‘Amen’ for her prayers. She should say, ‘O Allah, I appeal before You through every name that is Your name or with which You have named Yourself for any of Your creatures or have kept in Your hidden knowledge before You. I appeal before You through the greatest of Your great names and through every word that You revealed to Moses, through every word that You revealed to Jesus and through every word that You revealed to Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, cleanse me of this blood.’
If she wants to enter Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Masjid) or the Masjid of the Holy Prophet, she should do the same thing.

He (the Imam) said, ‘She should go to station of Jibril (Gabriel) which is under al-Mizab. This is his place wherefrom he would ask permission from the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘This is the place where she should pray to Allah, facing the direction of Ka‘bah and say the prayer about menses. She will be cleansed, by the will of Allah.’”
